stem: Which Andrew Carnegie quotation best explains why he funded libraries like the one in this photograph?

options.label: A
options.text: “Under the law of competition, the employer of thousands is forced into the strictest economies, . . . and often there is friction between the employer and the employed.”

options.label: B
options.text: “The price which society pays for the law of competition, like the price it pays for cheap comforts and luxuries, is . . . great.”

options.label: C
options.text: “The best means of benefiting the community is to place within its reach the ladders upon which the aspiring can rise.”

options.label: D
options.text: “This, then, is . . . the duty of the man of wealth: To set an example of modest, unostentatious living, shunning display or extravagance.”

visual_elements: Carnegie Library, Sault Sainte Marie, Michigan, c. 1908
Black and white photograph of a large stone library building with columns and steps leading to the entrance.
